newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mazda to boost output capacity for RVs.
newsitem.headline: Mazda to boost output capacity for RVs.

text.p: Mazda Motor Corp said on Monday it would raise its production capacity for recreational vehicles to meet good demand for its Demio and Ford Festiva Mini-wagon compact RVs.
It said it would partly modify its Ujina plant to increase the production capacity, which it aims to achieve in mid-May.
Ford Motor owns 33.4 percent of Mazda.
Production capacity for Demios and Festiva Mini-wagons at the Ujina plant in Hiroshima prefecture, western Japan, will rise to 10,000 units per month from current levels.

Mazda's production facility for Demios and its Festiva Mini-wagons now produces 9,000 units per month with overtime and holiday work to try to meet the buoyant orders. On standard hours the monthly production capacity is 7,000.

Mazda received about 50,000 orders for Mazda Demios and Ford Festiva Mini-wagons in the first four months or so since their launch on August 26 last year with a combined monthly sales target of 5,000.
